+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        # Deferred import: orientation imports Pose at module level.
+        from fleet_telemetry.orientation import normalize_quaternion, quaternion_from_euler
+
+        if self.qx is None or self.qy is None or self.qz is None or self.qw is None:
+            qx, qy, qz, qw = quaternion_from_euler(self.roll, self.pitch, self.yaw)
+        else:
+            qx, qy, qz, qw = normalize_quaternion(self.qx, self.qy, self.qz, self.qw)
+        object.__setattr__(self, "qx", qx)
+        object.__setattr__(self, "qy", qy)
+        object.__setattr__(self, "qz", qz)
+        object.__setattr__(self, "qw", qw)
findings.explanation: When a quaternion is supplied Pose keeps the caller-provided (or default 0.0) roll/pitch/yaw unchanged and only normalises q. Policy says Euler angles can remain as derived values computed from the quaternion. This leaves pose.yaw stale (e.g. quaternion-only construction yields yaw 0) while heading_deg/rotation_matrix use the quaternion, so pose.yaw and heading_deg diverge.
findings.suggested_fix: In the else branch after normalising q, derive roll, pitch, yaw with euler_from_quaternion(qx,qy,qz,qw) and object.__setattr__ them so Euler stays a derived view of the quaternion, as parse_frame already does.

+def _parse_covariance(raw: Any) -> tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]:

+    except TypeError as exc:

findings.explanation: Only TypeError is converted to TelemetryParseError; invalid numeric strings raise ValueError from float() and leak as ValueError, and degenerate quaternion raises ValueError in normalize_quaternion that is not wrapped, breaking the expected TelemetryParseError contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch (TypeError, ValueError) in _parse_covariance and wrap normalize_quaternion errors in parse_frame into TelemetryParseError.
